newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PetSec sees doubling in market cap.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PetSec sees doubling in market cap.

text.p: Petroleum Securities Australia Ltd managing director Terry Fern said the Gulf of Mexico producer and explorer planned to more than double its market capitalisation beyond A$1 billion in the next three years.
"We plan to become a A$1 billion to A$2 billion company," Fern said in an address to the Securities Institute of Australia on Wednesday.
He said this would be achieved by an aggressive drilling programme in the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Louisiana, with US$70 million earmarked for this in 1996/97 on 13 wells and two platforms.
PetSec had a market capitalisation of A$541.78 million in Wednesday afternoon trading based on its share price of A$5.10.
The company has 106.23 million shares on issue.

Fern said a recent research report by U.S. brokerage firm Petrie Parkman and Co had allocated an Australian dollar equivalent value to PetSec shares of A$7.40 to A$8.10 over the next 12 months. He said he agreed with this valuation.

The company's growth would be internally funded and would be achieved by remaining with its sights fixed on the shallow waters of the Gulf of Mexico. But the rise in market capitalisation could bring unwanted merger overtures, he said.
"I would prefer not (to be involved in takeovers) and I have looked at the consequences of a lot of corporate activity," Fern later told reporters.
"You don't quite know what you are buying."
While PetSec management owned about 30 percent of the stock, the company realised that once it reached its market capitalisation target of at least A$1 billion it would attract attention.
"I suspect that within the next year we will be approached by a number of these (rival producer) companies."
